1Purpose

This policy is the frame for the module at [Provider name]. It names the seven standards we work to and the policy that carries each one, the roles that run the module, and the rules that apply across the whole module. It sets no time limit and restates no commitment of its own: each of POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 holds its commitments, its clocks and its checks in one place. It is for families, our workers, the other services in a child's team, and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every child who receives early childhood supports from us, and their , from first contact until supports end.
  • Everyone who works for [Provider name] and has contact with those children or families: employees, contractors, students, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every place we work: the family home, early learning and school , community places, our premises, and phone or video sessions.
  • A sole trader or partnership registered for these supports, in the same way as a larger provider.

This policy is the shared frame for the module. POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 each set out one standard in full, with its own commitments, times and checks; nothing in this policy changes them. POL-CHS-01 Child Safe Policy sets the child safety rules for all our work with children; until it is written, the appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule.

3Commitments

C1

We will do what POL-ECS-02 The Child Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the child, s 56).

C2

We will do what POL-ECS-03 The Family Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the family, s 57).

C3

We will do what POL-ECS-04 Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (inclusion, s 58).

C4

We will do what POL-ECS-05 Collaboration Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (collaboration, s 59).

C5

We will do what POL-ECS-06 Capacity Building Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (capacity building, s 60).

C6

We will do what POL-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (evidence-informed supports, s 61).

C7

We will do what POL-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (outcome based approach, s 62).

4Ground rules

G1

A child's safety comes before everything else in this policy. A worker who is worried about a child acts on that worry first.

G2

A person with decides about the child's supports. We ask for the child's own views in a way that fits their age and how they communicate, and we record them.

G3

One route for every concern. A practice concern goes to the . A conduct or safety concern about a colleague or a manager goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive or an owner goes to the chair of the governing body, or in a sole trader's business to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. A child who may be at goes to the the same day, under PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). The person a concern is about never handles it.

G4

The time limits of the module are set in POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 and the procedures under them; the Module clocks table at the end of these ground rules reproduces them, and this policy sets none of its own. Where the law sets a shorter time, the shorter time applies.

G5

The appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule: the law of [state or territory] on who must report, the test, where, how fast, and the duty of every adult to tell police of child sexual abuse. POL-CHS-01, when written, holds the wider child safe standards and reportable conduct rules. The Quality Manager checks the schedule every 12 months and when the law changes.

G6

Each fact is held once. REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register is the one register for the module and holds dates, names, counts and record numbers. The forms hold the detail and the family's words.

G7

A family can say no to a , a referral, a team meeting or a question. Saying no is recorded and is never a reason to reduce supports.

G8

A complaint made by a child or family at any point is handled under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. A child's "stop" or "not happy" signal is a complaint the child can make in their own way.

G9

A sole trader holds every role except practice supervisor and independent contact for concerns. An outside practice supervisor with early childhood experience and the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register are the checks on the sole trader's own work.

G10

The is the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row. Where the family chooses a key worker from our team, the key worker is the plan lead, and when the key worker changes the plan-lead role moves with it the same day.

9Words we use

345 words
early childhood supports
supports for a young child with developmental delay or disability, and their family, under the registration class "early intervention supports for early childhood".
family
the parents, carers and other people who raise the child, as the family itself describes them.
parental responsibility
the legal authority to make decisions for a child. A court or child protection order can change who holds it.
support network
the relatives, friends, educators and others in the child's everyday life whom the family chooses to involve.
everyday routines
the things the child does most days, such as meals, play, bath time, getting dressed and going to early learning.
key worker
the one practitioner the family chooses as their main contact. Where the family chooses a key worker, that person is the plan lead.
team around the child
the family, our practitioners and the other providers who work together on the child's plan.
plan lead
the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row.
practice supervisor
the clinical supervisor of the early childhood practitioners.
practitioner drafting for the plan lead
the practitioner the plan lead asks to draft the plan under PRO-ECS-08. The plan lead stays accountable for the plan.
functional outcome
something the child will do in daily life, written so the family can see when it has happened.
coaching
helping a parent, carer or educator practise a strategy in their own routine, in place of doing it for them.
both clearances
an NDIS worker screening clearance, and the working with children check of [state or territory].
child safety lead
the role the Chief Executive names to receive every concern about a child and to see that reports are made.
risk of harm
the words this module uses for the reporting threshold. Our test is that you suspect on reasonable grounds that a child is at risk of harm. The appendix to POL-ECS-02 gives the exact term used in [state or territory].
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

docs.html:
1Purpose

This policy sets how [Provider name] assesses and supports each child in their , so they take part alongside other children. It is for families, our workers, the services around the child and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every child who receives from us, and their .
  • Every practitioner, and manager of ours who works with those children. This covers employees, contractors, students and volunteers.
  • Every place where the child's life happens: the family home, relatives' homes, early learning, school, playgroup, community places and our own rooms. It also covers phone and video sessions.
  • A sole trader or partnership registered for these supports, in the same way as a larger provider.

This policy does not bind early learning services, schools or other services. It sets how we work with them.

3Commitments

C1

We will assess how each child takes part in their everyday routines. We watch each routine in the place where it happens, with the people who are normally there. The interim plan (FRM-ECS-07 version 0) is agreed with the family within 10 of the first session, before the is signed, from the family record and the family's description of two or three routines, so and support start; the interim plan does not wait for the assessment. The first full plan does: we finish the assessment before it is approved, and the full plan is approved within 20 business days of the assessment being signed. Finishing the assessment is a for the first plan review.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 1, Procedure step 5, Procedure step 7, Procedure step 9, Procedure step 26, Procedure step 28.

C2

We will assess a child only with the agreement of a person with . We talk only to the people the family agrees to. We visit a place only when the family agrees and the child's controls line in REG-ECS-01 col I covers that type of , against the setting-type child safety risk assessment held in REG-RSK-01 Risk Register. Before the first visit to an early learning service, school or group we agree the visit with the setting's nominated supervisor.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 3, Procedure step 6, Procedure step 26.

C3

We will build each assessment from what the family tells us, what we see and what the child shows us, and record which is which. We use the language, interpreter and communication supports the family chooses.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (2). How we do it: Procedure step 4, Procedure step 5, Procedure step 9, Procedure step 10, Procedure step 7.

C4

We will use a standardised tool, or an assessment away from the child's , only for a stated reason. A tool the NDIA asks for is a stated reason. Only a practitioner qualified to use it may do so. We always turn the result back into what it means for the child's routines.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 11, Procedure step 26.

C5

We will give the family a summary of each assessment, in the language and form they choose, within 5 business days of the last visit. We correct it with them before it goes into the plan.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 24, Procedure step 25, Procedure step 26.

C6

We will agree with the family the routines where they most want the child to take part more. We write each as something the child will do in that routine and place, which anyone could see or hear.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 17, Procedure step 27, Procedure step 26.

C7

We will plan every support in the places where the child's routines happen. We deliver a support away from those places only for a reason about the child or the family, recorded in the plan with the family's agreement. The Service Manager signs off that reason at plan sign-off and at each plan review, at least every 6 months. There is no separate clock, and this is the one rule for the module.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 18, Procedure step 19, Procedure step 26.

C8

We will work, with the family's consent, with the and group leaders in the child's early learning service, school or group. Together we agree the changes that let the child join the same routines as the other children.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 12, Procedure step 13, Procedure step 14.

C9

We will tell the family their options within 5 business days if a service or community place excludes a child because of disability. Excluding means refusing the child, sending them home, cutting their hours or setting extra conditions. We offer help from an , and tell the Service Manager the same day.

Answers: Legislation (2), Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 15, Procedure step 16.

C10

We will find out with every family which community groups, services and agencies they are linked with. We build on those before we offer new ones. Links have one home in this module, FRM-ECS-03 Section G.

Answers: Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 20.

C11

We will help open each link the family chooses. We agree an action, a person and a date within 5 business days of the family naming the link. We share information only with consent, and ask the family within 10 business days of the action what happened.

Answers: Legislation (3). How we do it: Procedure step 21, Procedure step 22, Procedure step 23.

C12

We will review each assessment with the family at every plan review, at least every 6 months. We also review within 10 business days of a trigger, such as a change of setting. We record what changed in the child's participation, places and links.

Answers: Legislation (1), Legislation (2), Legislation (3), Legislation (4). How we do it: Procedure step 29, Procedure step 30, Procedure step 28.

C13

We will let only a practitioner who has been signed off lead an assessment. A signs them off after watching them lead one with a family, or, where a live observation cannot be arranged, after reviewing a recorded or co-visited assessment or the completed FRM-ECS-03 and summary for the practitioner's first two children, with a live observation within 6 months.

Answers: Legislation (1). How we do it: Procedure step 2.

4Ground rules

G1

The family decides. A no to an assessment, a visit, a question, a person or a service is recorded as the family's choice. It is never a reason to reduce the child's supports.

G2

A concern that a child is at is acted on the same day under PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). It comes before everything else in this policy.

G3

A parent, carer or educator is with the child at every visit.

G4

We take no photo, video or recording of a child without the family's written agreement on FRM-RGT-03 Photo, Video and Audio Recording Consent Form. We never photograph or film another child.

G5

We never ask a child, a brother or a sister to interpret. We use the interpreter the family chose.

G6

A video or phone session counts as being in the child's everyday place only when the child is in that place. The routine must be happening there.

G7

We never give or accept money, a gift or any other benefit for sending a family to a service. A worker who could gain declares it first under POL-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Policy.

G8

The family's words stay as they said them. We do not score a child against other children or against a test, and we do not describe a child by what they cannot do.

G9

Each fact is held once. FRM-ECS-03 holds the detail of the assessment. REG-ECS-01 holds dates, names and record numbers. FRM-INF-01 holds consent. FRM-ECS-02 holds the family's strengths and priorities.

G10

A concern about a colleague or a manager goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive or the owner goes to the chair of the governing body. In a sole trader's business it goes to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.

G11

A complaint from a child or family is handled the same day under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure.

G12

The times in this policy are outer limits. Where the law sets a shorter time, the shorter time applies.

educator

priority

key worker

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: each child has an of how they take part in their , in the places where they happen. Every support and community is then planned from it with the .

This procedure gives effect to POL-ECS-04 Policy (Early Childhood Supports), C1 to C13, and to ground rule G2.

2When and who

Start this procedure when:

  • the first session with a child is held, or about to be (steps 1 to 28)
  • a review is due, or a in Decision table 2 happens (steps 29 and 30)
  • a service or community place refuses or limits the child, at any time (steps 15 and 16).

Who acts:

  • The leads the assessment with the family and keeps the child's row. Where the family chose a from our team, that is the plan lead.
  • The Service Manager checks the sign-off, signs off the reason for each at plan sign-off and at each plan review, keeps the -type child safety risk assessments in REG-RSK-01 Risk Register, and checks each assessment.
  • Every worker who sees the child tells the plan lead what they see, and reports any concern about the child's safety the same day.
  • The Quality Manager samples assessments every 3 months under POL-ECS-04 Inclusion Policy (Early Childhood Supports).

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds every role except and independent contact. At step 26 a sole trader checks their own form against Decision table 3 and signs it.

A is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

3Before you start

  • You hold : your NDIS worker screening clearance and the working with children check of [state or territory]. They are verified in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register.
  • You have signed FRM-CHS-01 Child Safe Code of Conduct and Acknowledgement.
  • The child has a row in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register, and you have the family's priorities in FRM-ECS-02 Family Strengths, Needs and Priorities Record.
  • You have a blank FRM-ECS-03 Everyday Routines and Participation Assessment.
  • You have a blank FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form and a blank FRM-RGT-03 Photo, Video and Audio Recording Consent Form.
  • You have the family's communication preferences, or a blank FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form.
  • You have set aside time. An assessment takes more than one visit.

4Watch out

  • No agreement, no visit. A visit, call or record made without the agreement of a person with breaches the family's privacy and can break a court order.
  • The family's yes is for each person and place. A call or visit to someone the family did not name breaches their privacy and can end their trust in us.
  • A cannot wait for the form. A child who is at risk stays at risk while the assessment carries on.
  • A routine seen only in our rooms is not the child's life. Supports built on it may not fit the child's days, and the family may stop using them.
  • Other people's children. A photo or video that shows another child breaches that child's privacy and can put them at risk.
  • A test is not the assessment. A score used in place of the routines hides what the child can do at home and can lead to supports that do not fit.
  • A child left out is not the child's fault. A family that is not told its options may not know it can challenge the exclusion. The child loses time with other children that cannot be made up.

5Steps

Agree and prepare

Step 1

The plan lead

Open a new assessment and record why it is being done.

Start from the child's row in REG-ECS-01 and FRM-ECS-02. Write the record number and the reason. Name who will lead the assessment. For a review, go to step 29.

Result
One assessment is open for one child, with a named leader.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q1 to Q3
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the first session (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C1. Written on: Form Q1, Form Q2, Form Q3.

Step 2

The Service Manager

Check that the practitioner who will lead the assessment is signed off to lead one.

Look in REG-HRM-02 for the sign-off. A practice supervisor gives it after watching the practitioner lead an assessment with a family or, where a live observation cannot be arranged, after reviewing a recorded or co-visited assessment or the completed FRM-ECS-03 and summary for the practitioner's first two children, with a live observation within 6 months. If there is no sign-off, name a practitioner who has one. A newly trained practitioner leads only with the practice supervisor present or by one of those routes. A sole trader asks an outside practice supervisor to watch the first assessment, or to review a recording or the first two completed forms. Initial Q3 with the sign-off date, so the practitioner does not look it up.

Result
Only a signed-off practitioner leads, and the sign-off date is on the form.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q3; REG-HRM-02
Time limit
Before the first assessment visit (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C13. Written on: Form Q3.

Step 3

Warning. A visit, record or referral made without the agreement of a person with parental responsibility breaches the family's privacy. It can also break a court order.

The plan lead

Ask a person with parental responsibility to agree to the assessment, and to say who we may contact and where we may go.

Check REG-ECS-01 col F first, then ask the person named there. Say in plain words what the assessment is, who will visit, what you will write and who will read it. Say that the family can say no to any part, and that saying no does not reduce supports. Give them time to think. For a child in out-of-home care, ask the child protection agency who may agree. Go through early learning, school, health services, relatives and other providers one by one. Record each agreement on FRM-INF-01 and add a line to REG-ECS-01 col Q. Record each no as the family's choice.

Result
A person with authority has agreed, knowing what the assessment involves, and every contact and place is either agreed or refused.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q4 and Q5; FRM-INF-01; REG-ECS-01 col Q
Time limit
Before you contact anyone else or visit anywhere (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C2. Written on: Form Q4, Form Q5.

Step 4

The plan lead

Agree with the family how the child and each family member will take part.

Check REG-ECS-01 col G first and ask only what is missing. Ask what language they want, and book the interpreter they choose. Never ask a child, a brother or a sister to interpret. Ask about communication aids, the best times, and who should be there. For an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander child, ask whether the family wants a cultural support person involved. Ask too about a community-controlled service.

Result
The family can take part in their own language and way.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q6
Time limit
Before the first visit (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C3. Written on: Form Q6.

Learn about the child's days

Step 5

The plan lead

Ask the family to describe the child's week, and to choose the routines they want you to watch.

Check FRM-ECS-02 first so you do not ask twice. Ask where the child goes, how often and who is there. Include every home, relatives, early learning, school, playgroup, shops, parks, places of worship and cultural events. The family says who counts as family. Ask where they would like the child to go, or go more often, and what has stopped that. Start with the routines they rank highest and the ones they find hardest. If the family would rather you did not come to a routine, ask them to describe it or to share a video they took.

Result
You hold the family's own picture of the child's places and people, and a list of routines to watch.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q8 to Q10
Time limit
Before the first assessment visit (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C1, POL-ECS-04 C3. Written on: Form Q8, Form Q9, Form Q10.

Step 6

Warning. A place the child's controls line does not cover can put the child, and the other children in it, at risk.

The plan lead

Check that the child's controls line covers each type of place before you first visit it, and agree the visit with the setting.

Look in REG-ECS-01 col I. The child's controls line, agreed under PRO-ECS-02 step 2, must cover the type of place (home, early learning service or school, community place) against the setting-type assessment held in REG-RSK-01. If it does not, ask the Service Manager to extend it under PRO-ECS-02 step 2. Do not visit the place until it does. Before the first visit to an early learning service, school or group, agree with the setting's nominated supervisor: the date and time; who we are, and our working with children check for them to sight; where we will be, and the setting's sign-in and supervision rules; that we take no photos of other children and follow its photography and child-safe rules; and what we will share back with the family's consent (Q33). Note at Q7 that the controls line covers the place.

Result
No visit happens in a place the child's controls do not cover, and the setting knows about and has agreed to our visit.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q7; REG-ECS-01 col I
Time limit
Before the first visit to each type of place (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C2. Written on: Form Q7.

Step 7

Warning. A routine watched in our rooms shows how the child does in our rooms. A support built on it may not fit the child's life.

The plan lead

Watch each chosen routine in the place where it happens.

Go at the time of day the routine happens. Let it run as it normally does and join in only if the family asks. Watch what the child does, how long they stay with it, how they take part with other people and what the adults do. A parent, carer or stays with the child. Take no photo or video unless the family has agreed in writing on FRM-RGT-03 Photo, Video and Audio Recording Consent Form. Never film another child. Write at Q11 how you learned about each routine.

Result
You have seen each chosen routine as it really happens, or you have said why you have not.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q7 and Q11
Time limit
Within 30 business days of the family's agreement at step 3 (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C1, POL-ECS-04 C3. Written on: Form Q7, Form Q11.

Step 8

Warning. A child at risk of harm stays at risk if the concern waits for the form to be finished.

Any worker at the visit

If you see or hear anything that suggests the child may be at risk of harm:

Follow PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).

Make the child safe. Call 000 if there is immediate danger. Tell the the same day. That is the person our Chief Executive named to receive these concerns. Do not question the child, and never promise to keep a secret. The assessment waits until the child is safe.

Result
The child's safety is dealt with before anything else.
Record
FRM-ECS-01
Time limit
Straight away (our standard)
Step 9

The plan lead

Describe each routine with the family.

For each routine, write what the child does now and how much help they need. Write how they take part with other people, what helps and what gets in the way. Use what you saw and what the family told you. Describe the barrier in the task, the place, the timing or what other people expect. Do not list what the child cannot do. Ask the family, or the educator, how happy they are with the routine, from 1 to 5. Write who gave the rating.

Result
Each routine is described as part of the child's life, not as a test.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q12 to Q17
Time limit
Within 2 business days of each visit (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C1, POL-ECS-04 C3. Written on: Form Q12, Form Q13, Form Q14, Form Q15, Form Q16, Form Q17.

Step 10

Warning. A child who is asked questions they cannot answer will often say what they think you want to hear.

The plan lead

Record what the child shows or tells you they like, dislike and choose.

Watch what the child chooses, where they go and what they stay with. Use the child's own way to communicate: words, signs, pictures, gestures or behaviour. Ask the family what each sign means. Write it as the child showed it.

Result
The child's own view shapes what we call meaningful for them.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q18
Time limit
Within 2 business days of each visit (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C3. Written on: Form Q18.

Step 11

The plan lead

Record whether a standardised tool or an assessment outside the child's was used, and why.

Use a tool only to answer a stated question, and only a practitioner qualified to use it does so. A tool never replaces steps 7 and 9. If one was used, write what its result means for the child's routines, in plain words the family can use. If the result does not change a routine, say so.

Result
Any test is explained, and is tied back to the child's everyday life.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q19 and Q20
Time limit
Before the summary at step 24 (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C4. Written on: Form Q19, Form Q20.

Include the child with other children

Step 12

The plan lead

Note which routines at the early learning service, school or group the child shares with the other children.

Look at arrival, group time, meals, play, rest and outings. Note each routine the child misses or does apart, and why. Ask the family what they see. If the child goes to no setting, write what the family said at Q9.

Result
You know where the child is already included and where they are left out.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q26
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the visit (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C8. Written on: Form Q26.

Step 13

Warning. Information shared with an educator without the family's agreement breaches the family's privacy.

The plan lead

Ask the educator or group leader what helps the child and what they want help with.

Check Q5 first. Ask only if the family agreed. Tell the educator the family will read what they say. Ask which routines go well and where they need ideas or support. Write 'family did not consent', 'setting declined' or 'no setting' if so.

Result
The setting's knowledge is in the assessment, or the reason it is not.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q27
Time limit
Within 30 business days of the family's agreement at step 3, alongside the visit at step 7 (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C8. Written on: Form Q27.

Step 14

The plan lead

Agree with the family and the setting the changes that let the child join the same routines as the other children.

Change the routine, the place, the materials or the adult help, not the child. For each change, write who at the setting will make it and from when. With the family's agreement, show them how to do it inside the routine. If the setting needs a health or safety plan, the child's treating health practitioner writes it, within their qualification. A practitioner of ours writes one only inside their own scope of practice (for example a speech pathologist's mealtime plan), and never a medication or seizure plan.

Result
Each change has an owner at the setting and a start date.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q28
Time limit
Within 10 business days of step 13 (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C8. Written on: Form Q28.

Step 15

Any worker who learns of it

If a service or community place has refused the child, sent them home, cut their hours or set extra conditions because of disability:

Tell the Service Manager.

Say what happened, when, and what the family knows. The Service Manager decides with you what help we can give the family.

Result
The Service Manager knows and can help.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q29
Time limit
The same day you learn of it (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C9. Written on: Form Q29.

Step 16

Warning. A child left out because of disability loses time with other children that cannot be made up. A family that is not told its options may not know it can challenge this.

The plan lead

If a service or community place has excluded the child because of disability (step 15 has been done):

Tell the family their options, and offer help from an .

The options are to talk with the setting again, to ask the setting to seek help through the Commonwealth Inclusion Support Program, or to use the setting's own complaints process. The family can also contact an advocate, make a complaint under the Disability Standards for Education 2005 to the Australian Human Rights Commission, or go to the anti-discrimination body of [state or territory]. The family chooses, and may choose to do nothing. With the family's agreement we can give the setting a letter that says what the child needs to take part. Write the date the family was told, and the date you will check back with them, in Q29 and REG-ECS-01 col AJ.

Result
The family knows its options and has decided what to do.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q29; REG-ECS-01 col AJ
Time limit
Within 5 business days of learning of it (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C9. Written on: Form Q29.

Choose priorities and where supports happen

Step 17

The plan lead

Agree each participation with the family, and what will look like.

Start from the priorities in FRM-ECS-02. Ask which are about the child taking part in a routine, and where. Use the family's order and words. Most families choose 3 to 6. For each, ask what you would see or hear if it went well. Write it as something the child does in that routine and place, so anyone could see it. This becomes an outcome in FRM-ECS-07.

Result
Each priority is in the family's words, in a named routine and place, and can be seen.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q21 and Q22
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the last assessment visit (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C6. Written on: Form Q21, Form Q22.

Step 18

The plan lead

Agree with the family what we will try in each priority routine, who will do it between visits, and where.

Name the person: a parent, a grandparent, a brother or sister, or an educator. The place is where the routine happens. We join by video only when the child is in that place and the routine is happening. If the family wants a support away from the child's everyday places, use Decision table 1. Then write the reason, the family's agreement and the look-again date (the next plan review) at Q25.

Result
Every priority has a strategy, a person and a place.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q23 to Q25; REG-ECS-01 col M
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the last assessment visit (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C7. Written on: Form Q23, Form Q24, Form Q25.

Step 19

The Service Manager

If any support is planned away from the child's everyday places:

Sign off or refuse each support planned away from the child's everyday places.

Use Decision table 1. Sign off only a reason about the child or the family, with the family's agreement. The look-again date is the next plan review, no more than 6 months away, and you look again at each plan review; there is no separate clock. Our convenience is never a reason. If you refuse, tell the plan lead the same day, who plans the support in the place where the routine happens. Put the support, the reason, your sign-off and the look-again date in REG-ECS-01 col AI; col AE computes the earliest date.

Result
No support is delivered away from the child's everyday places without a reason, agreement, sign-off and a look-again date.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q25; REG-ECS-01 col AI
Time limit
Before the first support away from the child's everyday places, then at each plan review (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C7. Written on: Form Q25.

Build on community and support links

Step 20

The plan lead

Ask the family which groups, services and agencies they are linked with, and which links they want to make or strengthen.

Start from what the family already has, and ask how each is going. Build on a strong link before you offer a new one. Never push a link the family does not want. Write 'none right now' and ask again at the next review. Links have one home in this module, FRM-ECS-03 Section G: PRO-ECS-03 step 16 carries any link the family named on FRM-ECS-02 question 29 here, and nobody keeps a second list.

Result
You know the family's links, and which ones they want.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q30 and Q31; REG-ECS-01 col N
Time limit
Within 30 business days of the family's agreement at step 3, usually in the summary conversation (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C10. Written on: Form Q30, Form Q31.

Step 21

The plan lead

Agree with the family the action, the person and the date for each link they want, and what we may share.

Choose one action for each link. Give information. Introduce the family, with consent. Go with the family the first time. Share a summary, with consent. Or let the family do it, with our help if they ask. Name who does it and by when. Check what the family has agreed we may share. Add it to FRM-INF-01 and REG-ECS-01 col Q if it is not there.

Result
Each wanted link has an action, an owner, a date and a consent line.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q32 and Q33; REG-ECS-01 col Q and col AJ
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 20 (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C11. Written on: Form Q32, Form Q33.

Step 22

Warning. Information shared with a service the family has not agreed to breaches their privacy.

The person named at Q32

Carry out the agreed action for each link.

Check Q33 before you share anything. Share only what the family agreed, and only with that service. If the service has no place or does not suit the child, tell the family and write why.

Result
The family is connected, or has a clear next step.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q34; REG-ECS-01 col N
Time limit
By the date agreed at step 21 (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C11. Written on: Form Q34.

Step 23

The plan lead

Ask the family what happened with each link.

Ask whether the link was made, how it is going and what they want next. If it did not work, ask why. Write one result: connected, waiting, not suitable, or family changed their mind. A link that is waiting is checked again at each plan review. Update REG-ECS-01 col AJ.

Result
The family's view of each link is on record, with a next step.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q35; REG-ECS-01 col N and col AJ
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the action (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C11. Written on: Form Q35.

Give back and check

Step 24

The plan lead

Go through the summary of the assessment with the family, and change what is wrong.

The summary is one page: the child's places, each routine, the priorities, where supports will happen and the links. Use the language and form the family chose: written, spoken, pictures or translated. Use the interpreter they chose. Ask 'Does this sound like your child? Did we miss anything?' Change what is wrong. If you disagree, keep the family's words beside yours. If the family agrees without signing, write how at Q37. Record the form you gave and how the family showed they understood it.

Result
The family has the summary in a form they can use, and has said it is right or has corrected it.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q36 and Q37; REG-ECS-01 col T (summary line)
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the last assessment visit (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C5. Written on: Form Q36, Form Q37.

Step 25

The plan lead

Sign the form and send it to the Service Manager.

Check that no answer in Sections A to H says 'not yet asked'. Q34 and Q35 stay open until each link action is done and checked. Attach any report the family chose to share. Do not send a form until the family has seen the summary. The family signs or agrees to the summary (Q36 and Q37), not Sections A to H; you sign Sections A to H.

Result
The completed assessment is with the Service Manager for checking.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Sign-off
Time limit
Within 5 business days of giving the family the summary (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C5.

Step 26

The Service Manager

Check the assessment against Decision table 3, then sign it or return it with the reasons.

Check every row in the table. If a row fails, return the form to the plan lead with the row and the reason. The plan lead fixes it and sends it back within 5 business days. A sole trader checks their own form against the table and signs it. The independent contact reads a sample of 3 rows every 6 months.

Result
The assessment is signed as complete, or goes back with a reason.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Sign-off
Time limit
Within 5 business days of receiving it (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C1, POL-ECS-04 C2, POL-ECS-04 C4, POL-ECS-04 C5, POL-ECS-04 C6, POL-ECS-04 C7.

Step 27

The plan lead

Write each priority into FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan as an outcome, and each support's place as its setting.

Use the family's words and what taking part will look like. Write the place at Q24 as the setting for each support. A support away from the child's everyday places carries its reason and look-again date. Do not take the first full plan to the Service Manager for sign-off until step 26 is signed; the full plan is signed off within 20 business days of that signature. The interim plan (FRM-ECS-07 version 0) under PRO-ECS-08 is agreed with the family within 10 business days of the first session, from the family record and the family's description of two or three routines, before this assessment is signed, so and support start; it does not wait for the assessment; finishing the assessment is then a trigger for the first plan review (Decision table 2). PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets the rest of the plan.

Result
The plan and the assessment say the same thing.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q38; FRM-ECS-07
Time limit
Before the first full plan is signed off, and within 20 business days of the Service Manager's signature at step 26 (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C6. Written on: Form Q38.

Step 28

The plan lead

Enter the assessment in the child's row in REG-ECS-01.

Fill col L: the date, the settings observed and who took part. Fill col N for each link. Fill col M when the plan is agreed. Write the next review date at Q39, and put it in col L as the next due date and in col U; col AE computes the earliest date.

Result
The register shows the assessment, its next due date and the links.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q39; REG-ECS-01 col L
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the Service Manager's signature (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C1, POL-ECS-04 C12. Written on: Form Q39.

Keep the assessment current

Step 29

The plan lead

Review the assessment with the family, using Section I of a new version of the form.

Ask what has changed in each priority routine, and put the family's rating now beside the earlier rating. Ask what has changed in the child's places and in each link. Ask what to keep, change, stop or add. Confirm with the family who agrees for the child now. Use Decision table 2 for when.

Result
The family and the plan lead have agreed what stays, what changes and why.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q40 to Q42
Time limit
By the due date or the time in Decision table 2 (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C12. Written on: Form Q40, Form Q41, Form Q42.

Step 30

The plan lead

Carry each agreed change into FRM-ECS-07 and the register.

Update the plan under PRO-ECS-08. Update REG-ECS-01 col L, col N, col AI and col AJ. Set the next review date at Q39 and in col L and col U. If who agrees for the child has changed, update col F.

Result
The plan and the register match what the family agreed at the review.
Record
FRM-ECS-03 Q39; REG-ECS-01 col L
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the review (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-04 C12. Written on: Form Q39.

6Decision

Decision table 1: where to deliver a support (steps 18 and 19). The routine happens in an everyday place: the child's home, a relative's home, early learning, school, playgroup or a community place. The default is to deliver the support there.

IfThenApproval

The child or family needs something we cannot bring: a quiet space for a child overwhelmed by the setting, or equipment only our rooms haveDeliver it in our rooms. Write how the strategy will be carried back into the routineThe Service Manager signs off before the first session and again at each plan review. The family agrees. Look again at the next plan review, no more than 6 months away

Decision table 2: when to review (step 29). A plan review under PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) includes this review. The current assessment stays in force until the new version is signed.

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
The family says no to the assessment, a visit, a person or a questionRecord it at the question as the family's choice. Do not press. Offer another way: they describe the routine, or share a video they took. Supports continue. Ask again at the next review, or sooner if they raise it. If the family declines every visit, the plan can still be signed off. The assessment then rests on what the family told us, and col L says so
A person with parental responsibility cannot be reached, or two people who hold it do not agreeDo not visit. Tell the Service Manager the same day. The Service Manager speaks with the family within 2 business days. They explain that we can go on only when a person with authority agrees, and ask to see any court order or the family's recorded arrangement in REG-ECS-01 col F. Never take sides. Record the agreement at Q4
The child is upset by your being thereStop. Let the parent or carer lead. Come back at another time, or learn the routine from the family's own video. Never press a child to show you something
A planned visit does not happenWrite why at Q7. Offer another time within 5 business days. After two missed visits for the same routine, use the family's description or video and say so at Q11
The early learning service, school or group will not agree to a visit or to take partDo not go in. Write 'setting declined' at Q27. Tell the family and ask whether they want help to talk with the setting. Learn the routine from the family
The interpreter or communication support is not availableMove the visit to a time when it is. Do not use the child, a brother or a sister to interpret
The family wants a support away from the child's everyday placesUse Decision table 1 and step 19
A deadline will be missed, or has passedTell the family before the date, with the reason and a new date. Tell the Service Manager. The Service Manager puts the new date in REG-ECS-01 col L, col AI or col AJ, as it applies, within 2 business days; col AE computes the earliest date. The Quality Manager reports any assessment more than 20 business days late to the Chief Executive
The family disagrees with the summaryDo not record it as agreed. Write what they say beside ours, and their words stand where the two differ. The Service Manager meets them within 5 business days. Tell them how to complain under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure

The family or the child's circumstances change in the middle of the assessmentTreat it as a trigger in Decision table 2. Confirm at step 3 who agrees for the child before you go on
The plan lead is away for more than 5 business days, or leavesThe Service Manager names another signed-off practitioner within 2 business days. The new plan lead reads the open form and tells the family who they are
You see or hear something that suggests the child is at riskFollow step 8 straight away. The form can wait
Your concern is about a colleague or a managerTell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or the owner, tell the chair of the governing body. In a sole trader's business, tell the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. You can phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you
The family complainsHandle it the same day under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure

8Done means

The assessment is finished when all of these are true:

  • every answer in Sections A to H is filled, and none says 'not yet asked'. Q34 and Q35 are filled as each link action is done and checked
  • the family has the summary in the form they chose, and has said it is right or has corrected it
  • the Service Manager has signed the form
  • each priority and the place of each support is in the child's plan
  • each link the family wants has an action, a person and a date.

These records now exist:

  • the completed FRM-ECS-03, with its sign-off, in the child's file
  • the consent lines in FRM-INF-01 and REG-ECS-01 col Q for each person and service the family agreed to
  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01, with col L, col N, col AI and col AJ, and the earliest due date computed in col AE
  • the summary line in REG-ECS-01 col T for the summary given to the family
  • the outcomes and settings in FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan
  • after a review, a new version of FRM-ECS-03 with Section I.

9Quick card

134 words
  • Follow PRO-ECS-02 straight away if you worry that a child is at risk. Call 000 if there is immediate danger (step 8)
  • Get a person with parental responsibility to agree before any visit (step 3)
  • Visit a place only after the child's controls line covers it and the setting has agreed to the visit (step 6)
  • Watch each routine in the place where it happens (step 7)
  • Share nothing the family has not agreed to (step 22)
  • Get the Service Manager's sign-off before any support away from the child's everyday places (step 19)
  • Tell the Service Manager the same day if a service refuses the child (step 15)
  • Give the family the summary within 5 business days of the last visit (step 24)
  • Review at every plan review and at each trigger (step 29)

questions.hint: Describe the barrier in the task, the place, the timing or what other people expect. Do not list what the child cannot do.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 9.

questions.section: Section C: Everyday routines (one row for each routine)
questions.text: How happy is the family, or the educator, with how this routine goes?
questions.hint: Their own rating, where 1 is not at all happy and 5 is very happy. Say who gave it.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 9.

questions.section: Section D: The child's view and other assessment information
questions.text: What does the child show or tell us they like, dislike and choose?
questions.hint: By words, signs, pictures, gestures, behaviour, where they go and what they stay with. Ask the family what each sign means.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 10.

questions.section: Section D: The child's view and other assessment information
questions.text: Did we use a standardised tool, or an assessment outside the child's everyday places?
questions.hint: If yes: its name, the question it answers, who asked for it, who did it and where. Only a practitioner qualified to use it may do it. Write 'none' if so.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 11.

questions.section: Section D: The child's view and other assessment information
questions.text: What does that result mean for the child's everyday routines?
questions.hint: Plain words the family can use. Say which routine it changes.
questions.optional: Yes, only when no tool or outside assessment was used
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 11.

questions.section: Section E: Participation priorities (one row for each priority)
questions.text: Which routine does the family most want the child to take part in more, and where?
questions.hint: Start from FRM-ECS-02. Use the family's order and words. Most families choose 3 to 6.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 17.

questions.section: Section E: Participation priorities (one row for each priority)
questions.text: What will taking part look like?
questions.hint: Something anyone could see or hear, in that routine and place. This becomes an outcome in FRM-ECS-07.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 17.

questions.section: Section E: Participation priorities (one row for each priority)
questions.text: What will we try inside this routine, and who will do it between visits?
questions.hint: Name the person: a parent, a grandparent, a brother or sister, an <button type="button" class="term" data-term="educator" data-def="a person who teaches or cares for the child in a setting, or leads the group." data-source="POL-ECS-04">educator</button>.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 18.

questions.section: Section E: Participation priorities (one row for each priority)
questions.text: Where will we deliver the support for this priority?
questions.hint: Name the place. It is the place where the routine happens. Write 'video, with the child in the place' where we join by video.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 18. Recorded in: Register col M.

questions.section: Section E: Participation priorities (one row for each priority)
questions.text: If any support will be delivered away from the child's everyday places, why, who agreed, who approved it, and when will we look at it again?
questions.hint: Write 'all supports are in the child's ' if so. Use Decision table 1 in PRO-ECS-04. The reason is about the child or the family, never our convenience. The Service Manager signs off the reason at plan sign-off and at each plan review; the look-again date is the next plan review, no more than 6 months away.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 18, Procedure step 19. Recorded in: Register col M, Register col AE.

questions.section: Section F: Inclusion in early learning, school and groups
questions.text: Which routines at early learning, school or a group does the child do with the other children, and which do they miss or do apart?
questions.hint: Arrival, group time, meals, play, rest, outings. Say why for each one missed or done apart. If the child goes to no , write what the family said at Q9.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 12.

questions.section: Section F: Inclusion in early learning, school and groups
questions.text: What did the educator or group leader tell us helps, and what do they want help with?
questions.hint: Only with the family's consent. Write 'family did not consent', 'setting declined' or 'no setting' if so. The family reads what you write here.
questions.optional: Yes, only when there is no setting, or the family or the setting said no
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 13.

questions.section: Section F: Inclusion in early learning, school and groups
questions.text: What changes have we agreed with the family and the setting so the child joins the same routines as the other children?
questions.hint: Each change, who at the setting will make it, and from when. Change the routine, the place, the materials or the adult help, not the child. If the setting needs a health or safety plan, the child's treating health practitioner writes it, within their qualification; a practitioner of ours writes one only inside their own scope of practice (for example a speech pathologist's mealtime plan), and never a medication or seizure plan. Write 'no setting' if so.
questions.optional: Yes, only when there is no setting
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 14.

questions.section: Section F: Inclusion in early learning, school and groups
questions.text: Has any service or community place refused the child, sent them home, cut their hours or set extra conditions because of disability?
questions.hint: If yes: what happened, the date we learned of it, the date we told the family their options, whether they want an <button type="button" class="term" data-term="advocate" data-def="an independent person who helps a family speak up and be heard. We help the family find one. We do not choose for them." data-source="POL-ECS-04">advocate</button>, and the date we will check back with the family.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 15, Procedure step 16. Recorded in: Register col AE.

questions.section: Section G: Community and support links (one row for each link)
questions.text: Which community groups, services and agencies is the family linked with now, and how is each going?
questions.hint: Child and family health, doctor, early learning, playgroup, cultural or faith community, parent groups, library, sport, other providers, the family's NDIS contact. Check FRM-ECS-02 first.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 20. Recorded in: Register col N.

questions.section: Section G: Community and support links (one row for each link)
questions.text: Which link does the family want to make or strengthen?
questions.hint: Their words. Start from what they already have and from the places they would like the child to go. Write 'none right now' if that is their answer, and ask again at the next review.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 20. Recorded in: Register col N.

questions.section: Section G: Community and support links (one row for each link)
questions.text: What will we do to open this link, who will do it, and by when?
questions.hint: Choose the action, then name the person and the date.

controls.label: Choice
options: go with the family the first time
the family does it, with our help if they ask

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 21. Recorded in: Register col N, Register col AE.

questions.section: Section G: Community and support links (one row for each link)
questions.text: What has the family agreed we may share with this service?
questions.hint: What may be shared, with whom, and the date on FRM-INF-01. Write 'nothing to be shared' if so.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 21. Recorded in: Register col Q.

questions.section: Section G: Community and support links (one row for each link)
questions.text: When did we carry out the action, and what did we do?
questions.hint: Date, who did it, and what was shared and with whom.
questions.optional: Yes, until the action is done
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 22. Recorded in: Register col N.

questions.section: Section G: Community and support links (one row for each link)
questions.text: What did the family say when we checked, and what is the next step?
questions.hint: Date checked. Result: connected; waiting; not suitable; or the family changed their mind. Then the next step.
questions.optional: Yes, until the family has been asked
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 23. Recorded in: Register col N.

questions.section: Section H: Summary for the family
questions.text: When and how did we give the family the summary of this assessment?
questions.hint: Date; who went through it; the language; the form (written, spoken, pictures or translated); and how the family showed they understood it.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 24.

questions.section: Section H: Summary for the family
questions.text: What did the family say about the summary, and what did we change?
questions.hint: Ask 'Does this sound like your child? Did we miss anything?' Keep the family's own words beside ours if you disagree. Record how they agreed if they did not sign.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 24.

questions.section: Section H: Summary for the family
questions.text: When were the priorities and the place of each support written into the child's plan?
questions.hint: Date and version of FRM-ECS-07.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 27.

questions.section: Section H: Summary for the family
questions.text: When is the next review due?
questions.hint: No later than the next plan review date in REG-ECS-01 col U, and no more than 6 months after the date the summary was given. Enter it as the next due date in REG-ECS-01 col L.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 28, Procedure step 30. Recorded in: Register col L, Register col AE.

questions.section: Section I: Review (complete at each review)
questions.text: What has changed in each priority routine since the last assessment?
questions.hint: What the child does now. Put the family's rating now beside the earlier rating.
questions.optional: Yes, only at the first assessment
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 29.

questions.section: Section I: Review (complete at each review)
questions.text: What has changed in the child's places and in each link?
questions.hint: New places, places lost, <button type="button" class="term" data-term="link" data-def="a connection between the family and a community group, service or agency." data-source="POL-ECS-04">links</button> now active, links that ended.
questions.optional: Yes, only at the first assessment
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 29. Recorded in: Register col N.

questions.section: Section I: Review (complete at each review)
questions.text: What will we keep, change, stop or add, as agreed with the family?
questions.hint: Changes go into FRM-ECS-07.
questions.optional: Yes, only at the first assessment
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 29.

form.intro:
This form records how one child takes part in everyday life, in the places where they live, learn and play. It shows what helps, what gets in the way, and where the family wants the child to take part more. It is not a test and it has no score. The only number on it is the family's own rating at Q17.

The completes it with the family. An educator, a relative or another practitioner of ours can add to it. The family can read everything written on it. Health and safety needs the setting must know about (allergies, seizures, swallowing, mobility) are in the child's plan or a health practitioner's plan, not here; share those only with consent and never copy them onto this form.

When to complete it:

  • Sections A to H before the child's first full plan is approved. An interim plan under PRO-ECS-08, made within 10 of the first session, lets start before this is complete; finishing it is a trigger for the first plan review.
  • Section I at every plan review, in a new version of the form. A review is due at least every 6 months (our standard). A trigger in Decision table 2 of PRO-ECS-04 Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) also makes one due.
  • Section C has one row for each routine, Section E one row for each , and Section G one row for each link. Section G is the one home for community and service links in this module; FRM-ECS-02 question 28 holds only the family's own informal network.

Have ready:

  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register
  • FRM-ECS-02 Family Strengths, Needs and Priorities Record, so you do not ask the family twice
  • FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form
  • FRM-RGT-03 Photo, Video and Audio Recording Consent Form, blank
  • FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, if the family has one
  • any report the family has chosen to share.

Write the family's own words where they give them. Describe what happens in the routine and the place. If you do not know an answer yet, write 'not yet asked' and the date, and ask at the next contact. Sections A to H cannot be signed off with one left. The exceptions are Q34 and Q35, which you fill in when each link action is done and checked.

What happens next: each priority at Q21 becomes an outcome in FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan. Each link at Q32 gets an action, a person and a date. PRO-ECS-04 sets every step.
form.privacy:
Say this to the family before you start, in the language and way they use.

"We ask these questions to understand your child's everyday life, so our support fits into it. You choose what to tell us. You can skip any question, say no to any visit and stop at any time. Saying no will not reduce your child's supports.

We keep this record in your child's file. The people who work with your child read it. We share it with an educator or another service only if you agree. The one exception is where a law says we must share, for example to keep a child safe.

We take no photo or video of your child unless you agree in writing first. If you share a video with us, we watch it with you and keep a copy only if you agree. We never photograph or film other children.

You can read this record and ask us to correct it. Ask [privacy contact]."

Tell an educator, or any other person who adds to this form, that the family will read what they say.

[Provider name] handles this record under POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy and the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).
form.after:
• Plan lead: give the family the summary within 5 business days of the last visit (step 24, our standard).
  • Plan lead: sign the form. Send it to the Service Manager within 5 business days of giving the family the summary (step 25, our standard).
  • Service Manager: check it against Decision table 3, or return it with the reasons, within 5 business days of receiving it (step 26, our standard).
  • Plan lead: write the priorities and the place of each support into FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan. Do this before the first full plan is approved, within 20 business days of the Service Manager's signature (step 27, our standard).
  • Plan lead: enter the assessment in the child's row in REG-ECS-01 within 2 business days of the Service Manager's signature (step 28, our standard).
  • Quality Manager: every 3 months, trace a sample from the register row to this form. Ask 2 sampled families whether the summary sounded like their child.
  • The family keeps their copy of the summary. An educator or another service gets only the parts the family agreed to share.
  • Keep the form and every earlier version in the child's file for as long as REG-ECS-01 keeps the child's row (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years). REG-INF-02 Records Retention and Disposal Register (Rise version not yet written) holds any longer period the law of [state or territory] sets.

register.proves:
This register holds one row for every child who receives from [Provider name]. The row is the index to the child's file. It shows who the is, who is in the team, what the family agreed to, and when each plan, review and report was due and done.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 56 (1) to s 56 (4), s 56 (5)(a) and s 56 (5)(b).
  • Also s 57 (1) to s 57 (8), on the family.
  • Also s 58 (1) to s 58 (4), on , and s 59 (1) to s 59 (4), on collaboration.
  • Also s 60 (1) to s 60 (5), on capacity building, and s 61 (2), on practitioner skills.
  • Also s 62 (1) to s 62 (6), on outcomes.
  • Legal basis: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018, Schedule 5, clauses 3 to 9. Section 20(3), item 18 of those Rules applies Schedules 1 and 5 to early intervention supports for early childhood.
  • No NDIS instrument sets the columns of this register. The columns are our standard, built from the indicators.
  • Each fact is held once. The forms hold the detail and the family's words. This register holds the dates, the names, the counts, the record numbers and a one-line pointer to the form.
  • Clearances and training are in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. Intake and the service agreement are in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register (Rise version not yet written); until it exists, column F holds who has .
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years after supports end, or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard; NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years).
  • Retention where column J holds a record number: keep the row for 45 years (Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, recommendation 8.1; our standard). Check the child safe and records law of [state or territory] at adoption and before any row is destroyed.

Columns A to G and I are filled before the first session, and columns H and Y by the end of it. Column J stays blank until a record exists. Columns K to X and AH are filled as the plan is made and followed. Columns Z, AA and AD are filled when an interruption, a transition or an exit comes up. Columns AB, AC, AE, AF, AG, AI, AJ, AK and AL are kept current for every row.
register.entry:
1. The opens the row within 2 of the family accepting our offer (our standard). The Service Manager names the plan lead that day.
  2. Use one row for each child. Brothers and sisters each get their own row, linked in column AF.
  3. Fill columns A to G and I before the first session. Column J stays blank until a record exists. The first session does not go ahead while column I is empty for the type of it is in.
  4. Fill columns H and Y by the end of the first session.
  5. Fill every other column within 2 business days of the form or meeting that produces it (our standard).
  6. Write "not yet asked" with a date when a required answer is not known. Ask at the next contact with the family.
  7. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  8. Columns H, N, R, X, Z, AH, AI, AJ and AK hold dated entries. Add each new entry underneath the last one. Column AL holds one date, replaced at each check.
  9. The family's own words stay in the forms (FRM-ECS-02, FRM-ECS-03, FRM-ECS-05). This register holds dates, names, counts, record numbers and one-line pointers. Where a short phrase of the family's is entered, such as "none wanted" in column N, it is entered as it was said, signed or shown. Nobody tidies it.
  10. Column J takes record numbers only. Never write what was seen, said or suspected in this register.
  11. When the plan lead is away for more than 5 business days, the Service Manager names another worker to keep the row.
  12. When the system is down, complete the paper forms. Enter the row within 1 business day of the system coming back.
  13. A sole trader is the plan lead and keeps every row.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • column AD is filled and column AC says "exited"
  • the family has their final progress report and their copy of the last plan
  • column AA shows the handover was given, or the family's decision that none was wanted
  • every consent line in column Q has a withdrawn date or an end date
  • nothing in column AE, AI, AJ, AK or AL is still due.

• The plan lead and the key worker can see the rows of the children they work with.
  • The Service Manager, the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive can see every row.
  • A worker can see columns B, E, G, M, P, S, U and Y for the children they see. They cannot browse the register.
  • Column J shows record numbers only. Only the child safety lead, the deputy and the Chief Executive can open the forms behind those numbers.
  • A person with parental responsibility can ask to see their child's row and ask us to correct it. We answer within 10 business days (our standard).

  • Another provider in the team receives only what column Q allows.
  • An auditor or the NDIS Commission sees rows only as the law allows or requires.

Rows hold sensitive personal and health information about children. Keep the register in [system name], with a login for each person and a log of changes. Lock away any paper form.
